naming: The loader deserializes with YamlDotNet's CamelCaseNamingConvention and refuses any key it does not know.

keys.description: Optional grouping label (the source system) the platform files the flow's pipeline and runs under. A blank value counts as none.
Optional text describing what the dimensions are for.
The dimensions, at least one and at most 100, names unique ignoring case. Each reads every distinct value of one attribute of one kind's records, however many there are.

One dimension: the attribute whose distinct values it holds (`kind`, `query`, `path`), each exactly as the index holds it (a key), where a key's human-friendly label is read (`label`), and how each key is cleaned into the value it belongs to (`clean`).

Further facts of each key read the way its label is, each under a name, for a key that names an OSDU record: `attributes: { Country: [data.GeoContexts.GeoPoliticalEntityID, 'data[GeoPoliticalEntityTypeID*=GeoPoliticalEntityType:Country:].GeoPoliticalEntityName'], SpudDate: data.SpudDate }`. At most 20; a name is a letter, then letters, digits and underscores, at most 64, unique ignoring case, and none of `value`, `keys`, `key`, `records`, `filter`, `label`, `id`. A build reads them with the label, in the same searches where they start at the same records, and keeps each key's value of each (at most 256 characters) with the record it came from, indexed: values and keys are looked up by them (`attr=Country:Norway`), an attribute lists its values, a search picks keys by them, and a cached dimension carries the ones its `fields` name. A value that is itself a record reference is kept as the code its id ends with, its escapes decoded.

One attribute: a path of the record the key names, or a list of paths, each but the last reading the references the next records are found by, at most 3; every reference is followed, and the first record reached that holds a value at the last path gives the attribute's value. A path's segment holding objects can filter them: `[Property=text]` keeps those whose property equals the text, `[Property*=text]` those whose property contains it ignoring case, `[Property$=text]` those whose property ends with it ignoring case (`data[GeoPoliticalEntityTypeID*=GeoPoliticalEntityType:Country:].GeoPoliticalEntityName`).

The steps each key (or its label, when `label` read one) is cleaned by, in order, at most 20; the value is trimmed at the end. Written as a step's name (`trim`, `collapseSpaces`, `upper`, `lower`, `nfc`, `nfkc`, `foldSeparators`) or as a step with its settings (`replace`, `map`). Left out, each key's label, or the key itself, is its value, trimmed; a key that names an OSDU record and has no label starts as the code its id ends with, its escapes decoded (`dev:reference-data--UnitOfMeasure:us%2Fft:` is `us/ft`), so a value is ready for a drop-down.

One step: `trim` (white space removed at both ends), `collapseSpaces` (every run of white space one space), `upper` and `lower` (case by the invariant culture), `nfc` and `nfkc` (Unicode normalization), `foldSeparators` (letters and digits kept, every run of anything else one hyphen, lower-cased), `replace` (written `{ replace: { pattern, with } }`) and `map` (written `{ map: <dictionary> }` or `{ map: { dictionary, field, otherwise } }`). A step that leaves nothing, or a value longer than 256 characters, leaves the key out of every value with the reason kept on it.

A dictionary document of the repository looked up, found as `dictionaries/<name>.yaml` above the flow: a listed value is replaced by the entry's value, matched exactly, or ignoring case when that finds one entry. Written as the dictionary's name, or with its settings.
The dictionary's name: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`.
The entry's field that gives the clean value. Left out, the one field an entry holds beside its key (`value` for a dictionary of pairs).

What a value the dictionary does not list comes to: left out, it goes on as it is; `~`, the key is left out of every value; a text, it becomes that text. An entry that lists a value with no value leaves it out as well.
A regular expression replaced in the value. Run by .NET's non-backtracking engine, in time linear in the value: a backreference, a lookaround or an atomic group is refused when the flow is loaded.
The regular expression whose matches are replaced.
What each match is replaced by; `$1` names the first group. Write `''` to remove the matches.

Count each value's records exactly, with one count of the search per value whose keys could share a record. Where the attribute repeats in a record (a list, an array of objects) the index counts keys held, not records, so without this such a value's count is the sum of its keys' and marked as not exact.
Optional text describing the dimension.

The kind whose records are read, `authority:source:entityType:version`, wildcards allowed per segment (`osdu:wks:master-data--Wellbore:*`). For a property of `data`, a build reads the saved template of every kind the pattern matches in the partition, and every one must index the property the same way.

Where a key's human-friendly label is read, for a key that names an OSDU record (a reference such as `data.WellboreID`): a path of the record the key names (`label: data.FacilityName`), or a list of paths, each but the last reading the reference the next record is found by (`label: [data.GeoContexts.GeoPoliticalEntityID, data.GeoPoliticalEntityName]`), at most 3. Every reference a step reads is followed (at most 20 a key), and the first record reached that holds a value at the last path gives it; a path's segment holding objects can filter them, as an attribute's can (`[data.GeoContexts.GeoPoliticalEntityID, 'data[GeoPoliticalEntityTypeID*=GeoPoliticalEntityType:Country:].GeoPoliticalEntityName']`). A build finds the records by id through the search service, 500 ids a search, and cleans the label into the key's value; a key that names no record, a record the search does not hold, and one holding nothing at the path, have no label: such a key is valued by the code its id ends with, its escapes decoded (`us%2Fft` shows as `us/ft`), and the build's notes say how many and why. The key stays the id, so its filter and its value's filter find the records holding it. Left out, each key is cleaned into its value itself.
The most distinct values the dimension keeps, between 1 and 5000000: a build that finds more fails before it writes anything, since it holds the values in memory while it groups them.
The dimension's name: a letter or digit followed by letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, at most 100 characters. A run, a page, a filter and a cache type name the dimension by it.
The partitions of the flow the dimension is built in, when not all of them; left out, it is built in every partition the flow builds in.
One partition the dimension is built in, one the flow names (or, for a flow building in every registered partition, any partition).

The attribute, as a path from the record's root: any property search can match exactly. A property of `data` (`data.FacilityName`, `data.Curves.Mnemonic` inside a nested array, a value inside a flattened array, a list of values), or a property of the record itself: `id`, `kind`, `type`, `namespace`, `authority`, `source`, `version`, `createUser`, `modifyUser`, `createTime`, `modifyTime`, `collaborationId`, `acl.viewers`, `acl.owners`, `legal.legaltags`, `legal.otherRelevantDataCountries`, `legal.status`, `ancestry.parents`, `index.statusCode`, or a tag as `tags.<name>`. An array of objects without an `x-osdu-indexing` hint, an object and a value inside a nested array inside another are refused: search holds no exact value there.

Optional Lucene query narrowing the records read, with `{parameter}` and `{partition}` tokens. Left out, every record of the kind is read. The filters of keys and values select by key alone: combine them with this query where a search should read the same records (a composed search does).

The document kind: `dimension`, the distinct values attributes of OSDU records hold, each kept exactly as the search index holds it (a key: the text, or the id a reference names) and grouped under a human-friendly value (the label read from the record a key names, cleaned), with the search filter each key and each value stands for. The loader chooses the reader by it and refuses a document that declares no `flowType` or `documentType`.
The dimension flow's name: its pipeline identity, and the name its dimensions are kept under. A flow that builds in partitions keeps its dimensions per partition, shown as `name@partition`.

Optional: the flow's parameters, by name. `{name}` tokens are usable in a dimension's `query`; `{partition}` is always the partition the run builds in, so no parameter may be called `partition`. Values come from `--set name=value`, the run's values, or the schedule's `values`.
One parameter; `<name>` is the name its `{name}` tokens use. A run supplying a value for a name the flow does not declare is refused.
The value used when a run supplies none.
Text describing what the parameter is for.
When true, a run that supplies no value, for a parameter without a default, fails with "parameter 'name' is required". A scheduled fire supplies only the schedule's `values`, so give it one there.

The OSDU data partitions the flow builds dimensions in, hard-coded: each by its `data-partition-id` written literally, never a reference, at least one, at most 64, none twice. A run builds in one of them: the one it names, else the registry's default when the flow names it, else the flow's only one; `*` is refused. Left out, with no `data-partition-id` header, the flow builds in every registered partition. Each partition keeps dimensions of its own.
One partition the flow builds dimensions in, by its `data-partition-id`.

The HTTP settings (timeout, retry, rate limit, TLS, URL allowlist and response size), and `concurrency`: the tests evaluated at once, and the requests each has in flight. `reliability.parallelInterfaces` is refused.
A delivery flow's setting: rendered documents per work batch file. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: records claimed per ledger round trip when retrying records. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
The tests evaluated at once, and the requests (storage reads, reference lookups, bulk reads) one test has in flight. At least 1.
A delivery flow's setting: the member runs a large submission spreads over. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: below this many records a submission never fans out. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: how long a worker's lease on a record lasts. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: the target's declared request body ceiling (0 = not declared). The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
The largest response body read, in bytes. A larger response fails the request with a message naming this setting.
A delivery source's setting: how many of its interfaces run at once. An assertion flow runs no interfaces, so the loader refuses it here.
The most requests per second the flow sends to the platform; 0 means unlimited. Token requests are not limited.

A delivery flow's setting: renderers in the intake pipeline on one node, 0 to 256 (0 takes half the machine's processors, at least one). The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
How one request is repeated inline. Only requests that are safe to repeat are repeated, on 408, 425, 429, 503 and 504 and on a transport failure; 500 and 502 are not replayed.
The most attempts one request gets, the first included.
The wait between attempts: `exponential` doubles `baseDelayMs` per attempt, `fixed` waits `baseDelayMs` each time; both are capped at `maxDelayMs`.
The first wait between attempts, in milliseconds.

Whether a `Retry-After` the service sends is honoured. A requested wait within `maxDelayMs` becomes the floor of the backoff; a longer one is never shortened, so the request stops instead of waiting it out.
The longest wait between attempts, in milliseconds.
A delivery flow's setting: the first wait between a record's attempts across worker passes, in minutes. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: the longest wait between a record's attempts across worker passes, in minutes. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: statuses that hold a record instead of retrying it. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
One HTTP status code.
How long one HTTP request may take, in seconds.

The hosts requests may reach (an SSRF guard), checked on every request and every redirect hop. Empty allows any host the deployment's network policy reaches; token requests are not checked against it.
A host name, or `*.suffix` to match the bare domain and any subdomain of it. Compared ignoring case.
Whether the platform's TLS certificate is verified. `false` also needs `SQLFLOW_DELIVERY_ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS=true` on the node, or the run is refused.
The OSDU platform the dimensions are read from. A build only reads: nothing is ever written to OSDU.

How many groups the platform's aggregation returns: its `AGGREGATION_SIZE`, 1000 unless its operators changed it, between 10 and 10000. A build pages past it by value ranges, taking a range answered with fewer groups as complete, so this must not be more than the platform's setting; less only asks more often.

How requests to the OSDU platform authenticate, written as `target.auth` is on a delivery flow. Secrets are references only: ${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}. Left out, requests carry no credentials (type `none`).
keys.appliesWhen: Optional; written as `target.auth` on a delivery flow.

keys.description: The header an `apiKeyHeader` auth sends the key in.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is apiKeyHeader, which needs it.

keys.description: The secondary secret, as a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}): the username for `basic`, the client id for `oauth2ClientCredentials` (sent as `client_id` unless the token body names one).

The primary secret, as a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}), never a literal: the token for `bearer`, the key for `apiKeyHeader`, the password for `basic`, the client secret for `oauth2ClientCredentials` (sent as `client_secret` unless the token body names one).
keys.appliesWhen: Needed by bearer, apiKeyHeader and basic; used by oauth2ClientCredentials.

keys.description: The OAuth2 token endpoint: where a token is requested and how it is read from the answer. One token serves the run and is requested again shortly before it expires.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials, which needs it.

keys.description: The text put before the access token in the `Authorization` header.
When true, the client id and secret are sent as an HTTP Basic `Authorization` header on the token request instead of in its form body.

Extra form fields of the token request, by name. `grant_type` is `client_credentials` unless set here, and `client_id` and `client_secret` come from `secondarySecretRef` and `secretRef` unless set here.
One form field of the token request; `<name>` is the field name (such as `scope`). The value may be a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}), resolved before the request is sent.
An OIDC discovery document whose `token_endpoint` is the token URL. When set it is used instead of `url`; it may be a reference.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials; give this or url.

keys.description: The path of the access token in the token endpoint's JSON answer.
The token endpoint URL, usually a reference such as `${env:OSDU_TOKEN_URL}`.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials; give this or discoveryUrl.

keys.description: The auth scheme: `none`, `bearer` (a token as a reference), `apiKeyHeader` (a key in a named header), `basic` (username and password) or `oauth2ClientCredentials` (a token requested from `token`). Read ignoring case.
The text put before the secret in the header value of a `bearer` or `apiKeyHeader` auth. An OAuth2 token takes `token.applyPrefix` instead.
The base URL of the OSDU platform, usually a reference such as `${env:OSDU_URL}`.

Headers sent with every request. A flow that names its partitions, or builds in every registered one, may not name `data-partition-id` here: each run sets it to the partition it builds in. A flow that names neither builds in the partition this header names.
One header; `<name>` is the header name (`data-partition-id: dev`). A value may be a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}).
The search service's offset search, which aggregates a dimension's values and counts records (openapi search v2, POST /query).
The search service's cursor search, which a build scans the records of a range through when an aggregation cannot answer it (openapi search v2, POST /query_with_cursor).
